text:

distance. When a current of 3 A flows through

current of 2 A passes through 'Q', the flux
through 'P' is :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mutual induction

$𝜙_{q}=MI_{p}$

$10^{–3} = M(3)$

$\Rightarrow M=\frac{1}{3}\times 10^{-3}$

$𝜙_{p}=MI_{q}$

$\Rightarrow 𝜙_{p}=6.67\times 10^{-4}Wb$

text:
A metal wire of resistance 3 $\Omega$  is elongated to
make a uniform wire of double its previous
length. This new wire is now bent and the ends
joined to make a circle. If two points on this
circle make an angle 60° at the centre, the
equivalent resistance between these two points
will be :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
On stretching, the volume $V=Al$ of the wire stays constant, so $A=V/l$ and

$R=\dfrac{ρl}{A}=\dfrac{ρl^{2}}{V}\propto l^{2}$

Doubling the length multiplies the resistance by $2^{2}=4$, so the new wire has $R^{'}=4\times 3=12\Omega$.

Two points on the circle subtending $60^{\circ }$ at the centre divide it into arcs that are $\dfrac{60^{\circ }}{360^{\circ }}=\dfrac{1}{6}$ and $\dfrac{5}{6}$ of the length, with resistances $\dfrac{12}{6}=2\Omega$ and $\dfrac{5}{6}\times 12=10\Omega$.

The two arcs join the same two points, so they are in parallel:

$R_{eq}=\dfrac{2\times 10}{2+10}=\dfrac{20}{12}=\dfrac{5}{3}\Omega$

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

text:
Four point charges –q, +q, +q and –q are placed
on y-axis at y = –2d, y = –d, y = +d and
y = +2d, respectively. The magnitude of the

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Electric field at $p = 2E_{1}\cos θ_{1}$ $–2E_{2}\cos θ_{2}$

= $\frac{2Kq}{(d^{2}+D^{2})}\times \frac{D}{(d^{2}+D^{2})^{1/2}}-\frac{2Kq}{\left [(2d)^{2}+D^{2}\right ]}\times \frac{D}{\left [(2d)^{2}+D^{2}\right ]^{1/2}}$

$=2KqD\left [\left (d^{2}+D^{2}\right )^{-3/2}-\left (4d^{2}+D^{2}\right )^{-3/2}\right ]$

$=\frac{2KqD}{D^{3}}\left [\left (1+\frac{d^{2}}{D^{2}}\right )^{-3/2}-\left (1+\frac{4d^{2}}{D^{2}}\right )^{-3/2}\right ]$

Applying binomial approximation $\because$ d << D

$=\frac{2KqD}{D^{3}}\left [1-\frac{3}{2}\frac{d^{2}}{D^{2}}-\left (1-\frac{3\times 4d^{2}}{2D^{2}}\right )\right ]$

$=\frac{2KqD}{D^{3}}\left [\frac{12}{2}\frac{d^{2}}{D^{2}}-\frac{3}{2}\frac{d^{2}}{D^{2}}\right ]$

$=\frac{9kqd^{2}}{D^{4}}$

text:
The position vector of a particle changes with
time according to the relation
$\vec{r}(t)=15t^{2}\hat{i}+(4-20t^{2})\hat{j}$
 What is the
magnitude of the acceleration at t = 1 ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$⃗{r}(t)=15t^{2}\hat{i}+(4-20t^{2})\hat{j}$

Velocity is the time derivative of position:

$⃗{v}(t)=\frac{d⃗{r}}{dt}=30t\hat{i}-40t\hat{j}$

Acceleration is the time derivative of velocity:

$⃗{a}(t)=\frac{d⃗{v}}{dt}=30\hat{i}-40\hat{j}$

It is constant, so at $t=1$ its magnitude is

$|⃗{a}|=\sqrt{30^{2}+(-40)^{2}}=\sqrt{900+1600}=\sqrt{2500}=50$

Hence, the correct answer is $50$, which is Option A.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{T}{R}$ = Constant

text:
A wedge of mass M = 4m lies on a frictionless
plane. A particle of mass m approaches the
wedge with speed v. There is no friction
between the particle and the plane or between
the particle and the wedge. The maximum
height climbed by the particle on the wedge is
given by :-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initial condition can be shown in the figure
below


[IMG]


As mass $m$ collides with wedge, let both wedge and mass move with speed $v^{'}$. Then,


[IMG]

Given:

Mass of the wedge (M) = 4m

Mass of the particle (m)

Initial speed of the particle (v)

There is no friction.

Step 1 : Conservation of Linear Momentum

Before the collision, the momentum of the system is just the momentum of the particle because the wedge is at rest. After the collision, both the particle and the wedge will be moving. Let's denote the final common velocity as $v^{'}$. 

We can write the conservation of momentum as :

$mv=(m+4m)v^{'}$

which simplifies to 

$v^{'}=\frac{v}{5}$

Step 2 : Conservation of Mechanical Energy

We apply the conservation of energy before and after the collision. Before the collision, only the particle has kinetic energy. After the collision, both the particle and the wedge have kinetic energy and the particle has potential energy due to its height h on the wedge.

We can write the conservation of energy as :

$\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\frac{1}{2}(m+4m)v^{'}^{2}+mgh$

which simplifies to 

$mv^{2}=(m+4m)v^{'}^{2}+2mgh$

Substituting equation (1) into this equation gives

$v^{2}=5v^{'}^{2}+2gh\Rightarrow \frac{4}{5}v^{2}=2gh$

which simplifies to 

$h=\frac{2v^{2}}{5g}$

So, the maximum height climbed by the particle on the wedge is given by $\frac{2v^{2}}{5g}$.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D :

$\frac{2v^{2}}{5g}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th April Evening Slot
